newsitem.title: USA: LPGA GOLF-KING WINS DINAH SHORE BY TWO STROKES OVER TSCHETTER.
newsitem.headline: LPGA GOLF-KING WINS DINAH SHORE BY TWO STROKES OVER TSCHETTER.

text.p: Betsy King methodically wore down the competition to win the Nabisco Dinah Shore for the third time in her 20-year career on Sunday.
King closed with a final-round, one-under-par 71 at Mission Hills Country Club to finish at 12-under par 276, two strokes ahead of Kris Tschetter.
Kelly Robbins, who was three strokes ahead of King with eight holes to play, played the back nine in four-over-par 40 and fell to third place, three strokes behind King.

"When I was down three, I thought I was not going to win the tournament," said King, who earned $135,000. "I figured Kelly was going to win. I was watching what was happening to Kris (Tschetter) and Amy (Fruhwirth) to see what I needed to do to finish second."
Robbins bogeyed the 12th and 13th holes, then lost the lead at 14, when King made a 15-foot birdie putt. Robbins doubled-bogeyed the par-4 15th hole to fall from contention.
The victory was the 31st of King's career, but her first since winning the ShopRite LPGA Classic in 1995. It was the sixth major championship of a career that has landed her in the LPGA Hall of Fame.
"Once in a while the old guard can still do it," said King, 41. "I'm just trying to get back to where I was. I'm definitely hitting the ball better. I feel like I can play again."

Robbins' bid to win a second major championship ended with the double-bogey. She muffed a chip from the back of the green, the ball barely reaching the putting surface. Then she badly misread her par putt and missed her bogey putt coming back.
"Half of the round was pretty good," Robbins said. "When I hit it back in a couple of spots it got the best of me. You never like to finish that way."
